claim.quote: This observation provides world best direct detection constraints on WIMP-proton spin-dependent scattering for WIMP masses $>$20 GeV/c$^{2}$ and demonstrates significant sensitivity for spin-independent interactions.

key_value.note: Total exposure over three bubble-nucleation thresholds.

name: First dark matter search results from a 4-kg CF$_3$I bubble chamber operated in a deep underground site

summary.plain: The same chamber, moved two kilometres underground to SNOLAB with 4.0 kg of CF3I, set the best limit of its time on spin-dependent WIMP-proton scattering for heavier WIMPs.
summary.technical: 4.0 kg CF3I in the SNOLAB J-Drift, September 2010-August 2011: 553 kg-days over three nucleation thresholds (437.4 kg-days effective for single bubbles); 20 single nuclear-recoil candidates and 3 multiple-bubble events; an internal neutron background estimated to account for five single-recoil events; alpha rejection >99.3% (Phys. Rev. D 86, 052001).

title: First dark matter search results from a 4-kg CF$_3$I bubble chamber operated in a deep underground site
why_it_matters: The abstract says the observation gives world-best direct-detection constraints on WIMP-proton spin-dependent scattering for masses above 20 GeV/c^2.
